chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Bardu Ali, the front man of Chick's band
summary: Bardu Ali fronted the band as a showman and dancer; later Babe Wallace fronted it before Benny Carter declined to take over.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: One thing I want to ask. Oh, I want to clear the record. I was incorrect.
Helen Ward preceded Martha Tilton and Helen Forrest followed.
Yeah.
I get the Helens mixed up. Helen Forrest, F-o-r-r-e-s-t.
Before we get any further in this -- you know, we're going to come back into some of this. But let's talk about Bardu Ali.
Bardu Ali?
Yeah. He was like the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
He was like the conductor of the band before I -- He was in the band before I get there (Unaudible). He was --
What did he do in the band? Was he a musician or..?
No.
Okay.
He was just like --
Like a stand-up in front of the band.

All right, like a Lucky Millinder. He was flashy like Lucky Millinder, but not as flashy as Mike Lucky. Lucky would go way out, you know. Jump off the piano and jump down and do a split -- all that kind of stuff -- with his tails on. Bardu Ali could do a split, turn over, and do all the things like Lucky. He knew the tempos of the band. He looked good in front of the band. He was a nice looking man -- very nice
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

looking guy. Made a good attraction in front of the band.

But then, when the band started -- when we got into this heavy music and stuff, you know --

Then after he left, we got Babe Wallace. I think Babe Wallace came in after Chick Webb -- when I took the band -- when I really took the band over, they got Babe Wallace to front the band.

And he worked, I think, one theater date -- the Apollo. We went to Pittsburgh -- we played a big date there. A big center there. It was a big date.

Bardu got -- we had at that time --

You know, I had took the band -- I hadn't taken the band to the coast that time. When we had came back we had played out with Chick Webb.

That's when we had played all around Chicago, the Midwest. We came back to Pittsburgh -- we did the Famous Door same as you do (inaudible) couple a weeks in there, or something like that.

Then we went to the Roseland -- we played at the Roseland. Then after that, Moe Gale

wanted to call a halt. We wanted to try to get Benny Carter to take the band over. And Benny didn't want to take the band over, because he wanted changes. He wanted it (Inaudible) Benny Carter's band with Ella Fitzgerald (Inaudible).
Where did Bardu Ali come from? I mean, he was with Chick when you got there.
Bardu was a New York boy.
Was that a name he picked up or was that --
That was his --
-- his real name?
That was his real name. Nice looking guy. Like a showman. He was a dancer, I think.
Do you know anything about his background, about where he --
No. All I knew is that he -- He didn't do any singing. I know he was a nice looking guy, he danced -- he could dance, you know -- tap dance or something. I didn't know too much -- the only time
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I knew Bardu Ali was when I came back from off the road (later on (Unaudible)) and they wanted me to join the band.
Chick Webb sent him up to get me, because he knew me.
That's how you got in the Chick Webb's band?
Yeah. He sent him up to get me to join the band. That was in '36 when I came back into New York.
